newsitem.title: USA: Hess plans cracker expansion at St Croix.
newsitem.headline: Hess plans cracker expansion at St Croix.

text.p: Amerada Hess Corp still plans in October to expand its catalytic cracker at its Caribbean refinery on St Croix in the U.S. Virgin Islands, taking the unit down for up to six weeks, a company spokesman said.

"It will be the first turnaround since October 1993," said Hess spokesman Carl Tursi, referring to the unit, which will process 125,000 barrels per day (bpd) of feedstock at the end of the maintenance project, up from 110,000 bpd currently.
Tursi said the upgrade, previously announced in the company's latest annual report, will likely begin in mid October and last up to six weeks into November.

Tursi said the cat cracker expansion is part of the refinery's ongoing shift away from residual fuel to lighter products like gasoline. The cracker can use residual fuel as a feedstock to produce gasoline.
He said the refinery now produces about 50 percent gasoline and one-third distillates, compared to about 50 percent residual fuel about 20 years ago, he said.
The St Croix refinery has throughput capacity of 500,000 bpd, but has run in recent years run at an annual average of about 430,000 bpd.
